raw_response:
I'm 71 this year. I've been farming this land since I was 16 — my father taught me, and now it's just me and the old woman working it. Our son is in Shijiazhuang doing construction work, sends a bit of money home when he can, but he can't help on the farm. We've got 2.2 mu, not much, but it's our land and I know every corner of it.

This year I'm putting chili on the whole plot again, same as the last three years. Wheat and maize? That's for people with machines and more land. For 2 mu, chili gives better money per mu, and I can manage it with my own two hands. Last year I got about 2200 jin per mu, sold for around 1.8 yuan per jin. Old Zhang down the lane switched to stevia and lost money — I'm not making that mistake.

I bought chili seedlings from the market in town, the kind with thick stems. Cost me about 220 yuan total for 2.2 mu. I know some folks save their own seeds, but my neighbor Mrs. Liu did that two years ago and her peppers were small and got that wilt disease. Not worth the risk. The shop girl said these hybrid ones grow strong here.

For fertilizer, I spread about half a bag of that compound stuff — the one they call 15-15-15 — before I transplant. That's about 25 kg per mu. Then when the plants flower, I throw down some urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That's all. I know the young extension fellow says put more, but fertilizer costs too much now, and honestly my soil is pretty good after 50 years of putting manure on it. My son wanted me to buy that water-soluble fertilizer, but it's 80 yuan a bag! No. Too much fertilizer makes the plants grow big leaves but the peppers don't turn red fast — I've seen it with my own eyes.

Water — I pump from the well. Four times this year, I reckon. Once right after transplanting, once when the flowers come, and twice when the peppers are swelling up. Pumping costs diesel money, so I don't waste water. If it rains good, I skip one. Last August it rained plenty, so I only pumped three times.

Pesticides — I have to. The aphids always come, and there's that root rot. I spray three times with whatever the shop recommends. I can't read the bottles, never learned, but the shopkeeper knows me and shows me which picture matches the bug.

Labor — me and the old woman do most of it. Planting takes us three days, hoeing and weeding another few days, and picking goes on for months because you pick chili four or five times. In August when the peppers all come at once, I hire Old Li's nephew for two or three days — he wants 150 yuan a day now! But my back can't bend like it used to. For 2.2 mu I hoe the soil myself and mix in the base fertilizer by hand. No tractor for this small plot, that's just silly.

If the weather is normal and no big disease comes, I expect about 2000 to 2200 jin per mu — around 1000 kg. Last year was good. Year before was a bit less because of that dry spell in July.

All in all, I'm spending about 1200 yuan on seedlings, fertilizer, pesticide, diesel for the pump, and hired help. Sounds like a lot when you say it out loud, but we need the income. The old woman says we should eat less meat to save money, but I say we need the chili money more.
